verdict.reason: All five findings of the first review are closed by their mechanism, with a test that fails on FREEZE-A1 and passes on FREEZE-A2. But the mechanism of the QE-R7A1-03 fix (and the C5 rule of FREEZE-A1 it extends) does not check that a newer return reports the same break. A second, separate break that begins in a week an earlier return re-planned is treated as a correction of the first: its return starts from the state before the first break. The first return's re-entry is erased (return steps, run RETURN mode), and the athlete goes back to pre-break doses after a 16-day break: 1 set at RIR 4 becomes 3 sets at RIR 3 at the pre-break known load, and the long run goes from 20-45 to 70-75 minutes (QE-R7A1-09, HIGH, material). The same missing identity makes a second short break reuse the first one's easy slot, so its own first quality run stays hard (QE-R7A1-10, MEDIUM, material). Across the week boundary the defect is new in FREEZE-A2; inside the same week it is already present in FREEZE-A1, and my first review missed it. FREEZE-2 has neither. A new HIGH blocks under FOUNDER_REQUEST §13.

newFindings.class: C5 supersession: a later, separate break is read as a newer report of the earlier break (return identity); state preservation and return ceiling
newFindings.mechanism: returnAfterPause reads prior = program.weeks[pauseWeek].startBeforeReturn ?? stateTrace[pauseWeek] (r6-adaptation.mjs:626) for any return whose break begins in a week where an earlier return stored startBeforeReturn (a MODERATE or LONG return that re-planned its own week, :651). Nothing checks that the newer report is about the same break: its interruption dates against the earlier one's, or its start against the earlier return's report day. For a separate break that began after re-entry started, the newer return starts from the state before the first break. It erases the re-entry state that the first return set and the athlete executed: returnStep, the run RETURN mode and its returnTo. SHORT then 'resumes last completed doses' from pre-break doses. Origin: the same-week variant came with FREEZE-A1's C5 reading (pauseWeek === w), which my first review did not find. The cross-week variant came with FREEZE-A2's QE-R7A1-03 fix, which applied my required change as written. FREEZE-2 reads stateTrace[pauseWeek], the re-entry start, and has neither variant.

newFindings.requiredChange: Identify the break a return reports: record its interruption, or at least its report day, with startBeforeReturn. Read startBeforeReturn only for a newer report of that break, for example one whose break begins before the earlier return's report day or overlaps its interruption. Otherwise start from the stored start of the break's week (the re-entry the athlete was doing). Tests: two separate breaks in the same week and across the week boundary keep the first re-entry; the QE-R7A1-03 and C4/C6 correction tests keep passing.

newFindings.class: C4/C5 (D58): the short-return easy slot's identity is not tied to its return (same root cause as QE-R7A1-09)
newFindings.mechanism: shortReturnEasy (r6-composition.mjs:114) takes as its slot any session whose explanation is the easy-slot text, before looking for the first quality slot still ahead of its report. The composeWeeks carry (:203) uses the same test. A second, separate short break in a week whose quality slot an earlier short return already eased (now history) therefore takes that old slot as its own. Nothing is carried, and the first quality slot after the second break runs as planned. FREEZE-A1 and FREEZE-2 gave no easy slot in either case (the D58 defect). FREEZE-A2 fixes the single-return case but not this one.
newFindings.reproduction: reviews/qe-a2-P14-second-short-break-easy-slot.mjs (outputs .A2, .A1copy, .F2). Default program (quality on Tuesday); weeks 0-2 executed. Week 3 Monday 06:00: a 6-day short return eases Tuesday's quality run, which is run and reported. A second break Wednesday-Friday (3 days) is reported Saturday 06:00, then the weekly review. FREEZE-A2: week 4 Tuesday stays QUALITY THRESHOLD 41, and the only easy slot is w3-run-d1 (the first break's). The same second break alone on FREEZE-A2: week 4 Tuesday runs EASY 41.
newFindings.requiredChange: Tie the eased slot to the return that made it (for example the return's event id on the row and in the adaptation). A newer report of the same break keeps its slot; a separate short break gets its own. Test: two separate short breaks in one week. The dose reading stays with the SSCTR (D58).

notReadyRecord.rootCause: Return supersession (C5) has no break identity. 'A newer report of a break' is implemented as 'any return whose break begins in a week an earlier return re-planned' (startBeforeReturn), and as 'any slot already eased' (the easy-slot explanation). A separate, later break is therefore read as a correction of the earlier one.
notReadyRecord.whyNotClosed: The same-week variant entered with FREEZE-A1's C5. My first review, the handler grids and the tests did not exercise two separate breaks. The cross-week variant entered with the A2 fix of QE-R7A1-03, which my first review specified without a same-break condition. The single correction cycle is spent (FOUNDER_REQUEST §11).
notReadyRecord.smallestNextMission: One bounded fix in returnAfterPause and shortReturnEasy/composeWeeks: record the break a return reports, use startBeforeReturn and the earlier eased slot only for a newer report of that break, and otherwise start from the stored re-entry and give the new short break its own slot. Tests: two separate breaks (same week, across the week boundary) and two separate short breaks in one week, plus the existing correction tests. Then a narrow re-check that re-runs qe-a2-P13, qe-a2-P14, qe-a2-P02 and qe-a2-P09.
